ground_truth.title: State v. Marcus Ellison
ground_truth.location: Midland, Heartland General Hospital, Financial Services Department
ground_truth.charge: First‑degree extortion of a medical facility

defendant.name: Marcus Ellison
defendant.background: Long‑time employee at Heartland General Hospital, former CPA, promoted to senior finance manager in 2017; known for meticulous budgeting but has a history of financial disputes with staff

victim.name: Heartland General Hospital
victim.description: Publicly funded community hospital with annual budget of $120 million

ground_truth.what_really_happened: In early March, Marcus Ellison discovered an unauthorized $350,000 expense claim filed by a colleague. Rather than report it, he demanded that the hospital’s Chief Financial Officer (CFO) personally cover the discrepancy or face a fabricated lawsuit threatening to expose a minor regulatory violation. The CFO complied, paying $50,000 in cash to Marcus, who then returned the money to the original claimant. The CFO later realized the extortion and reported Marcus to the police. Marcus was arrested on March 12, 2024, and charged with extortion.

evidence.name: Bank Transfer Record
evidence.description: Electronic record of $50,000 transfer from CFO’s personal account to Marcus Ellison’s corporate account on March 4, 2024
evidence.truth_note: The transfer directly links Marcus to the payment requested; the account details match those used by Marcus during his tenure

evidence.name: CFO’s Testimony Transcript
evidence.description: Recording of CFO’s sworn statement detailing the extortion request and subsequent payment
evidence.truth_note: The CFO’s account is a direct source of the extortion claim, corroborating the timeline and the demands made by Marcus

evidence.name: CFO’s Office Email Correspondence
evidence.description: Emails between CFO and Marcus discussing the “sensitive matter” and the “situation” requiring “discretion”
evidence.truth_note: The email content reflects a conversation about the undisclosed discrepancy and uses language implying coercion

evidence.name: Surveillance Footage
evidence.description: Security camera footage of CFO entering Marcus’s office on March 3, 2024, showing a brief conversation
evidence.truth_note: The footage captures the CFO’s presence but does not show any verbal exchange; the conversation could have been about routine budgeting concerns

evidence.name: Hospital Payroll Ledger
evidence.description: Ledger entry indicating a $350,000 expense approved by an employee with an error flag; no record of reimbursement to that employee
evidence.truth_note: The ledger shows an anomaly but the error flag was added after the payment, indicating the system was used to conceal the discrepancy; the ledger alone does not prove Marcus’s intent

evidence.name: Witness Statement of Nurse Lydia Park
evidence.description: Statement that Nurse Park heard Marcus’s name mentioned in a private conversation about finances
evidence.truth_note: The statement is based on overheard audio; no direct reference to extortion is present, making it possible that Marcus was discussing routine budget concerns

witnesses.name: CFO Alicia Monroe
witnesses.role: Chief Financial Officer of Heartland General Hospital
witnesses.knows: Details of the extortion request and payment, timeline of events
witnesses.bias: Professional obligation to expose wrongdoing, personal stake in protecting hospital reputation

witnesses.name: Nurse Lydia Park
witnesses.knows: Hears Marcus’s name during private conversation about finances
witnesses.bias: Personal dislike for Marcus due to prior billing disputes
witnesses.lie_reason: May exaggerate Marcus’s behavior to protect her own standing
